headword: {職務質問|しょくむしつもん}

definitions.explanation: When a police officer stops a person on the street to ask questions about their identity, destination, or activities. A routine law enforcement practice in Japan, often abbreviated as 職質 (shokushitsu).

examples.japanese: {夜道|よみち}で{職務質問|しょくむしつもん}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I was stopped and questioned by the police on a dark road at night.

examples.japanese: {自転車|じてんしゃ}に{乗|の}っていたら{警察|けいさつ}に{職務質問|しょくむしつもん}された。
examples.english: I was stopped and questioned by the police while riding my bicycle.

examples.japanese: {深夜|しんや}に{繁華街|はんかがい}を{歩|ある}いていると、{職務質問|しょくむしつもん}を{受|う}けることがある。
examples.english: If you walk around the entertainment district late at night, you might be stopped and questioned by the police.

notes:
USAGE:
{職務質問|しょくむしつもん} is very commonly abbreviated to {職質|しょくしつ} in casual speech. It is a routine practice in Japan — police may stop pedestrians or cyclists, especially late at night, to ask questions and check identification.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {職務質問|しょくむしつもん}を{受|う}ける (to be stopped and questioned)
- {職務質問|しょくむしつもん}をする (to conduct a stop and question)
- {職務質問|しょくむしつもん}される (to be subjected to police questioning)

ABBREVIATION:
{職質|しょくしつ} — very common in everyday conversation.
- {職質|しょくしつ}された (I got stopped by the cops)

RELATED WORDS:
- {不審者|ふしんしゃ}: suspicious person
- {身分証明書|みぶんしょうめいしょ}: identification card
